author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Dr Graeme Groom, a British orthopaedic surgeon who has volunteered in hospitals across Gaza more than 40 times, says a problem with shortages of medicine in the war-torn enclave is that it sounds “almost benign”.

“We have colleagues who are in Gaza every month, and last night, a colleague sent an urgent request for an antifungal drug called amphotericin,” he told Al Jazeera on the sidelines of the Al Jazeera Forum in Doha, Qatar.

“She wanted this for an 18-year-old girl who had a very rare fungal infection, a mucormycosis, as a consequence of diabetes, multiple comorbidities, poorly treated because of the shortages. And her very last message was, “This is an emergency. The fungus is eating her face,” Groom said.

“So when we talk about the shortages and we talk about the lists that are zero stock, both of medicine and surgical equipment, it doesn’t sound quite as dramatic, but the individual impact is absolutely huge,” he concluded.

Cold War shadows fall across Latin America as US-backed coups shatter democracies, spark brutal dictatorships, covert operations and revolutionary resistance.

It describes the Brazilian military's 1964 overthrow of President Joao Goulart, driven by American fears of agrarian reform and "another Cuba", which forced activists like Jean Marc von der Weid into exile.
In Chile, President Salvador Allende's peaceful socialist experiment faced secret economic blockades before General Augusto Pinochet's military coup in 1973 established his brutal regime.

With more than 90 per cent of votes counted, Thailand's conservative Bhumjaithai Party has won a clear victory in the general election, securing over 190 seats in the new parliament.

The reform-minded People's Party faces a third term in opposition, whilst former ruling party Pheu Thai came a distant third and has limited bargaining power in coalition talks.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Japan’s Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has promised to cut taxes and keep her cabinet intact as she celebrated her Liberal Democratic Party’s (LDP) landslide victory in Sunday’s general election.
Takaichi’s pledge on Monday came as projections by the NHK broadcaster showed the conservative LDP securing 316 seats in the 500-member National Assembly and winning a “historic” two-thirds majority in the lower house.
The win gives Takaichi a strong mandate to push her promised tax cuts and a $134 bn stimulus package. 
She says the plan won't endanger the nations finances.
But the country has one of the biggest debt burdens among wealthy nations.
Financial markets have been volatile because they're worried about how Japan will fund the increased spending.

Seijiro Takeshita is the Dean at the University of Shizuoka's Graduate School of Management, Informatics and Innovation.
He says Takaichi is using debt to fund expansion, rather than relying on previous austerity measures.

title: Japan’s Takaichi vows to deliver on tax cuts after LDP’s ‘historic’ win

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Moderate socialist Antonio Jose Seguro has been elected president of Portugal with roughly two-thirds of the vote, defeating far-right rival Andre Ventura. Despite the decisive margin, nearly half of eligible voters abstained, and Ventura's Chega party has emerged as the main opposition force in parliament after less than a decade. The presidency is largely ceremonial, but Seguro faces the challenge of easing social tensions over living costs whilst trying to stem rising populist support.

Al Jazeera's Natacha Butler reports from Lisbon.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Iranian authorities have arrested four people on charges of attempting to “disrupt the country’s political and social order” and working “for the benefit” of Israel and the United States during the antigovernment protests of January.
The detainees, who were arrested on Sunday, included three prominent reformist politicians, according to Iranian media.
They are Azar Mansouri, head of Iran’s Reform Front, Mohsen Aminzadeh, a former diplomat, and Ebhrahim Asgharzadeh, a former parliamentarian.

The fourth remains unnamed.
Iran’s judiciary accused the group of “organising and leading extensive activities aimed at disrupting the political and social situation” at a time when the country faced “military threats” from Israel and the US, according to the official Mizan news agency.
The individuals had done their utmost “to justify the actions of the terrorist foot soldiers on the streets”, it said.
Iran’s Reform Front confirmed the arrests in a statement on X.

Al Jazeera’s Tohid Asadi report
title: Iran arrests prominent reformist politicians, cites links to US, Israel
